name: John Muir Trail Thru-Hike
tagline: For hikers thru-hiking the 211-mile John Muir Trail between Yosemite Valley and Mount Whitney over two to four weeks.
description: Assumes a July-September thru-hike of about 18-25 days, southbound from Yosemite or northbound from Whitney Portal, with two to four resupplies. Covers the continuous-trip permit honored by Yosemite, Inyo National Forest and Sequoia-Kings Canyon, mandatory bear canisters, Whitney Zone waste rules and high-pass conditions. Adapt the resupply count, snow gear and insulation to your start date and pace.
season: July-Sept (snow lingers on passes into July)
considerations: One continuous-trip wilderness permit is honored by every agency on the route and is issued by the agency where you start: Yosemite (Happy Isles 15/day, Lyell Canyon 30/day, with a 45/day Donohue Pass exit quota) or Inyo NF (Whitney Portal lottery Feb 1-Mar 15; as of 2026).

Allowed bear canisters are required in all of Yosemite, Donohue Pass to Reds Meadow, Duck Lake to Lake Virginia, Dusy Basin, Pinchot to Forester Pass, Kearsarge, Rock Creek/Cottonwood and the Whitney Zone; counter-balance hangs are legal only where canisters are not mandatory.
Whitney Zone: pack out solid human waste in the waste kit issued with your permit between Guitar Lake and Whitney Portal; Inyo charges $15/person for Whitney Zone permits plus a $6 fee (as of 2026).
Campfires are banned above 9,600 ft in Yosemite, 10,000 ft in the Ansel Adams Wilderness and SEKI, and 10,000-10,400 ft in the John Muir Wilderness, plus many lake basins; check current restrictions.

Resupply: General Delivery post offices in Yosemite Valley (year-round) and Tuolumne Meadows (mid-June to mid-Sept); commercial caches at Reds Meadow, Vermilion Valley Resort and Muir Trail Ranch need advance booking and fees (verify current terms).

Camping limits include 2-night maximums at Dusy Basin, Charlotte and Kearsarge Lakes, Woods Creek to Vidette Meadow (1 night per lake between Dollar Lake and Glen Pass) and Crabtree/Guitar Lake; no camping at Timberline Lake, Shadow Lake or within 1/4 mile of Thousand Island and Garnet Lake outlets.

Expect afternoon thunderstorms, altitude (Whitney is 14,505 ft), early-season snow and swift stream crossings, and mosquitoes through July; no surface water above about 12,400 ft on the Whitney Trail.
Inyo quota season is May 1-Nov 1; 60% of its permits release 6 months ahead and 40% two weeks ahead on Recreation.gov (as of 2026).

items.text: JMT wilderness permit from the agency where your hike starts
items.note: Yosemite lottery for Happy Isles/Lyell Canyon with Donohue exit; Inyo lottery for Whitney Portal starts (as of 2026).

items.text: Whitney Trail Crest exit or Whitney Portal start reserved on your permit
items.note: Trail Crest exit quota is 25/day; Whitney Portal starts use the Feb 1-Mar 15 lottery (Inyo NF, 2026).

items.text: Printed, signed permit and Whitney waste kit picked up at the permit station
Resupply plan: boxes sent to Tuolumne PO, Reds Meadow, VVR or Muir Trail Ranch
items.note: Confirm current deadlines, fees and pickup hours with each location.

items.text: Transport plan: YARTS/ESTA buses, shuttles or car shuttle between trailheads
Itinerary with daily mileage, camping limits and bailout trailheads shared with a contact
Acclimatization night at a mid-elevation campground before starting
items.note: Whitney Portal, Onion Valley and Horseshoe Meadows campgrounds sit at 8,000-10,000 ft.

items.text: Travel or rescue insurance
Allowed bear canister sized for your longest carry
items.note: Only models on the Yosemite/SEKI allowed list; store 50 ft from your sleeping area with the lid closed.

items.text: Food for the longest leg plus one extra day, repackaged
Resupply buckets or boxes sealed, labeled with name and ETA
Cash or card for resupply pickup fees and store purchases
Fuel allocation per leg and a spare lighter
Lightweight tent or tarp with bug netting
Sleeping bag or quilt rated to 15-25 F
Insulated pad (R-value 3 or higher)
Pillow and earplugs
Trail runners or boots, broken in
Wool or synthetic socks (3 pairs)
Rain shell plus rain or wind pants
Puffy jacket
Fleece or mid-layer
Sun hoodie and hiking shorts or pants
Warm hat and liner gloves
Sun hat and sunglasses (dark lenses for snow)
Camp or stream-crossing shoes
Town clothes in a resupply box
Water filter plus backup chemical treatment
items.note: Surface water can carry pathogens; filter, boil or treat everything.

items.text: Capacity for 2-3 liters, 3 liters for Whitney summit day
items.note: No water above about 12,400 ft on the Whitney Trail after snowmelt.

items.text: Stove, fuel and lighter
Pot, spoon and mug
Electrolyte mix
Cook and wash 100 ft from water; strain and scatter dishwater
JMT map set or app with offline maps
Compass or GPS device
Satellite messenger
items.note: Strongly recommended; report overdue hikers to the Inyo County Sheriff (760-878-0383).

items.text: Headlamp with spare batteries
First aid kit with blister care and altitude medication
Sunscreen and SPF lip balm
items.note: Reapply often; UV is intense above 10,000 ft.

items.text: Insect repellent and head net
Trekking poles
Microspikes or ice axe for early-season passes
Repair kit: tape, needle and thread, pad patches
Knife, whistle and signal mirror
Battery bank and cables (recharge at resupplies)
Pack liner or dry bags
Human waste kits: 1-2 per person per day in the Whitney Zone
items.note: Pack out used kits and drop them in the bins at Whitney Portal.

items.text: Summit-day plan: start early and turn around when storms build
Extra layers for wind and cold at 14,505 ft
Acclimatization schedule and knowledge of altitude sickness signs
Trowel; bury waste 6-8 in deep, 100 ft from water, trails and camps
items.note: Except in the Whitney Zone, where everything is packed out.

items.text: Pack out all toilet paper and hygiene products
Trash bag for all packaging; nothing burned or buried
Camp on durable surfaces 100 ft from water and obey posted camping limits
Fires only where allowed, in existing rings, drowned cold; prefer no fire
Hand sanitizer; urinate 100 ft from water and camps
